A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PathEval research. All 19 pages of each, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original VLM benchmark evaluations, perception experiments, fine-tuning results and encoder analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds a human-performance study in Appendix F.

M1.justification: PathEval construction, descriptor-based pair selection, VLM prompting, fine-tuning and encoder-probing procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same PathEval coverage: 14,550 instances, 15 scenarios and 2D/3D representations, alongside the same simplified perception tasks. Appendix F samples existing tasks without introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds four human annotators as comparators to GPT-4o: two authors and two external participants. The existing VLM, random-baseline and vision-encoder comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 60-example evaluation subset, comprising two examples per scenario in each of 2D and 3D, evaluated by four annotators and GPT-4o. Existing splits, training settings and model-evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The label-bias tests, descriptor and segment-complexity analyses, encoder probes, memorization study and failure examples are unchanged. Appendix F adds a human baseline comparison, without a separate new ablation, robustness test or error analysis.

E5.justification: The five-repeat attribute-abstraction procedure in Appendix D.1 is unchanged. Appendix F reports individual annotator scores without adding confidence intervals, formal significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Appendix F adds human accuracies ranging from 0.73–0.90 in 2D and 0.60–0.76 in 3D, versus GPT-4o's 0.53/0.47 on the sampled subset. These are additional subset results; the existing results in Tables 1–13 and Figures 1–5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, pair-selection normalization and seven path-descriptor definitions and formulas in Appendix B are unchanged. No new theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, vision-bottleneck claim, limitations of end-to-end fine-tuning and recommendation for task-specific encoder adaptation.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly qualifies benchmark difficulty by noting that 3D comparisons can challenge humans, despite all four annotators outperforming GPT-4o on the subset. Existing interpretations of model failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 already links to the PathEval GitHub repository. v4 retains that destination, displays the code URL explicitly and adds a separate Hugging Face dataset link; existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and 84 cited works are unchanged. Changed reference back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short Appendix F and replaces the combined access footnote with separate code and dataset footnotes. The existing prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds an unnumbered human-versus-GPT-4o table on PDF page 17 and slightly reflows the opening pages following the footnote expansion. Existing numbered tables and figures retain their displays.

improvement.justification: Appendix F supplies a previously missing human reference for interpreting benchmark difficulty, and the separate dataset link improves access information. The gain is limited by the 60-example sample, four annotators including two authors, and absent uncertainty estimates despite the word 'significantly.' The core experimental evidence remains unchanged.
